my-new-fj60-with-1hdt.ai_summary: A 1982 FJ60 had its original 2F gas engine and manual transmission replaced with a 1HD-T diesel and automatic transmission sourced from an 80-series, originally installed new in 1990 and still running as of the 2012 thread. The owner reported death wobble at highway speed and was troubleshooting stock FJ60 tach incompatibility with the diesel engine.

complications.detail: Death wobble at ~90 kph, initially suspected wheel balance
Large aftermarket transmission cooler left no room for a front-mount intercooler
Stock 4000-rpm FJ60 gas tachometer incompatible with diesel tach signal

my-new-fj60-with-1hdt.title: My new FJ60 with 1HDT

sema-h55f-water-air-ic.ai_summary: A 1986 FJ60 being built as a SEMA 2023 vehicle received a turbocharged 1HD-T (UFI 18G turbo) with a water-air intercooler and H55F 5-speed manual, plus a new transfer case. On initial startup the builder saw white smoke and engine shaking, which forum members attributed to air trapped in the fuel system rather than a fundamental swap defect.

complications.detail: White smoke and engine shaking on first startup, diagnosed as air in the fuel system during priming
Questions raised about secondary fuel filter setup and glow plug function for cold starts

sema-h55f-water-air-ic.title: 60 series 1hdt swap help

2f-to-1hz-31s.ai_summary: A 1987 FJ60 conversion from the factory 2F gas engine to a 1HZ diesel paired with an H55F 5-speed, retaining stock 3.70 gears and axles. One participant reported 21+ mpg at 70-75 mph highway cruising while loaded, running 31-inch tires. Builders discussed 24V-to-12V electrical fixes, radiator/fan-shroud modification, and moving the exhaust from the driver to passenger side to fit the diesel engine.

complications.detail: 1HZ is 24V while FJ60 is 12V; options discussed included voltage converters or rewinding starter/alternator to 12V (~$75)
Radiator lower port did not align with 1HZ; builder cut/turned the port and fabricated a custom fan shroud
Exhaust exits passenger side on the 1HZ versus driver side on stock FJ60, requiring custom piping

2f-to-1hz-31s.title: FJ60 2f to 1HZ

back-in-a-60-series.ai_summary: Build thread for a 1987 FJ60 (already lifted, on 33-inch tires, ARB bumper, roof rack) planning a diesel swap; early posts show the builder still weighing 1HDT/H55, 1HZ/H55, and Isuzu 4BD/H55 combinations rather than a confirmed completed 1HZ install. Toyota diesel engines quoted at $6k+, offset partly by reselling the original H55F/splitcase; forum consensus favored an H55F input-shaft swap as the path for 1HZ compatibility.

complications.detail: H55F input shaft swap required for 1HZ compatibility, described by an experienced builder as the trickiest part of the job
Cost-benefit debate: $6-7k diesel engine cost weighed against resale value versus a non-restoration build

back-in-a-60-series.title: Back in a 60 series - 1HZ Swap
back-in-a-60-series.transmission: H55F (retained from gas donor); still evaluating 1HDT/H55, 1HZ/H55, or Isuzu 4BD/H55 combinations

1985-6-0-ls-swap.ai_summary: 1985 FJ60 swapped with a 6.0L LQ4 (pulled from a Chevy 2500 Express van with ~70,000 miles) paired to a rebuilt 4L65E automatic, retaining the stock FJ60 transfer case via a custom transmission-to-transfer-case adapter. The original 2F/3FE petrol engine made roughly 140hp; no dyno figures were reported for the LS. Cooling was the biggest headache, later resolved with a larger dual-pass radiator.

complications.detail: Initial CSF radiator/dual SPAL fan setup ran 210-220F under load; replaced with a Griffin 31x19x3 dual-pass radiator and 160-degree thermostat, bringing steady temps down to 170-175F
Front driveshaft clearance to the transmission, exhaust, and oil pan was tight; required oil pan modification and moving the engine forward in the bay

1985-6-0-ls-swap.title: 1985 FJ60 -> 6.0 Liter LS Swap Build Thread

overdue-5-3-swap.ai_summary: FJ60 Land Cruiser rebuilt around a 5.3L GM LS-family V8 swap (started late 2014) as part of a full restoration including a strip-down, TRD Pro Cement color change, and full interior redo. The specific LS variant, transmission, and performance figures were not detailed in the visible posts, but the builder fabricated custom engine-management and steering hardware.

complications.detail: Fabricated a custom ECU shelf from 16-gauge stainless steel mounted to the driver's inner fender
Fabricated a high-pressure power steering coupler to mate the GM power steering pump to the Toyota steering gearbox

overdue-5-3-swap.title: Overdue Build Thread - Fj60 5.3 swap

wirings-and-gauges.ai_summary: Owner of a 1986 FJ62 inherited a partially completed 1HD-T diesel swap and was finishing the wiring/instrumentation, since the diesel's VR (variable reluctance) tach signal is incompatible with the stock gas tachometer. Other members pointed to a Shift Kits Australia signal converter and a Dakota Digital Hall-effect sensor as working solutions used on similar 1HZ/1HD-T swaps.

complications.detail: 1HD-T's VR sine-wave tach signal incompatible with stock gas tachometer, requiring a signal converter
Brake fluid and clutch reservoir warning sensors left unconnected after the swap

wirings-and-gauges.title: FJ62 with 1HDT wirings and gauges

durban-rebuild-and-swap.ai_summary: An in-progress, heavily documented rebuild-and-1HZ-swap of a 1987 FJ62 in Durban, South Africa, replacing the factory 3F petrol engine with a reconditioned 1HZ diesel. Builder sourced a 75-series bellhousing and the correct 21-spline input shaft/flywheel needed to mate the diesel to the H55F gearbox, while also addressing significant body rust and a cracked cab mount caused by deteriorated engine cushions.

complications.detail: Petrol H55F uses a 10-spline input shaft incompatible with 1HZ; required 21-spline fine-pitch shaft and correct flywheel
Cab-mount crack found, attributed to deteriorated engine cushions; welded repair pending new bushings, plus significant gutter/fender rust requiring donor FJ60 panels

durban-rebuild-and-swap.title: FJ62 (1987) rebuild, and 1HZ diesel swap
durban-rebuild-and-swap.transmission: H55F manual with 75-series bellhousing adapted for 1HZ - requires 21-spline fine-pitch input shaft (33311-60170) and 1HZ/HD-T flywheel

steves-offroad-conversion.ai_summary: A completed, professionally-installed (Steve's Off-Road, TN) 1HZ/H55F conversion into a 1988 FJ62, sold with 13,500 miles on the conversion and full receipts. Electrical system was converted from 24V to 12V using OEM Toyota parts, driveshafts were reworked, and the front axle was rebuilt and re-geared to 3.70. Owner reported worst-case 20 mpg and best-case 30 mpg, averaging about 24 mpg, with no drivability issues noted.

complications.detail: Converted 24V 1HZ electrical components (alternator, starter, fuel cut solenoid) to 12V using OEM Toyota parts
Driveshafts professionally reworked; front axle rebuilt and re-geared to 3.70
Factory A/C intact but new hoses needed for the factory mount to function

steves-offroad-conversion.title: FS: 1988 FJ62 1HZ/H55F diesel conversion, daily driver

3fe-to-1hdt-insight.ai_summary: Owner of a 1991 gas (3FE-powered) 80-series Land Cruiser sought guidance on swapping in a 1HD-T (or 1HD-FT/12H-T alternatives), with experienced members recommending H150/H151 5-speed manuals as most desirable, welding in HDJ80 engine mounts, and estimating roughly $5,000 for engine plus supporting parts. This is a planning/advice thread rather than a documented completed build.

complications.detail: Requires welding HDJ80 engine mounts into the FJ80 frame
Disagreement among members on whether firewall cutting is needed for clearance

3fe-to-1hdt-insight.title: Need insight on 3FE to 1HDT swap
3fe-to-1hdt-insight.transmission: H150/H151 5-speed manual (discussed) or retained factory automatic

93-converted-for-sale.ai_summary: A completed 1993 FZJ80 1HD-T conversion, listed for sale for roughly $18,000 CAD in parts/labor (excluding the vehicle), used the diesel's A442F ECT automatic upgraded with an 'Extreme Valve Body' for tighter shifts, a Walbro 6065 fuel lift pump to prevent injection-pump cavitation, and ceramic coating on the exhaust manifold/turbo dump for heat management. The seller reported about 20 mpg highway when loaded (24 mpg best recorded) and no cooling, reliability, or driveline problems, selling only because they were starting a new conversion on a 1997 truck.

complications.detail: Electrical integration described as 'pretty involved' but manageable with correct JDM parts and factory documentation
Added a Walbro 6065 lift pump to prevent injection pump starvation/cavitation

93-converted-for-sale.title: 1HD-T Converted US 93 FZJ80 for sale
93-converted-for-sale.transmission: A442F ECT automatic with upgraded valve body

93-swap-done-a442f.ai_summary: A 1993 FZJ80 was converted to a 1HD-T diesel paired with the diesel's A442F automatic transmission, requiring extensive rewiring done in collaboration with another forum member reading factory wiring diagrams. The builder described the diesel as pulling as hard as the factory 1FZ-FE gas engine, while acknowledging some loss of seat-of-the-pants acceleration feel; other members warned about high EGTs on long grades.

complications.detail: Extensive rewiring required, done via manual diagram-reading, plotting, and soldering
Forum members warned EGTs can run very hot on long grade climbs, recommending an EGT gauge

93-swap-done-a442f.title: another 93 FZJ80 1HD-T swap done...

97-conversion-ect-planning.ai_summary: Thread discusses planning a 1HD-T conversion into a 1997 FZJ80, focused on transmission/ECU compatibility: pre-August 1992 A442F transmissions use hydraulic/cable control while later ones are electronically controlled (ECT), and the 1997 FZJ80's combined engine/transmission computer complicates integrating an ECT-controlled diesel automatic. No confirmed completed build outcome is documented in the visible thread content.

complications.detail: Matching ECT transmission electronics to the 1997 FZJ80's combined engine/transmission ECU requires specific harness sourcing (from 1993-94 models) or an aftermarket solution (~$750)
Warning that imported used 1HD-T engines may need inspection/rebuild before use given added stress from mountain driving

97-conversion-ect-planning.title: 1 HD-T FZJ80 Conversion

hdj81-complete-swap-for-sale.ai_summary: A completed 1HD-T diesel swap (1992-chassis, informally referred to by the seller as 'HDJ81') listed for sale for $12,000, including a full 3-inch exhaust and 24V electrical system, with the seller noting it was still running in the truck and available to test drive before purchase. No performance figures or complications were disclosed in the listing.
hdj81-complete-swap-for-sale.title: For Sale - Hdj81 complete 1HD-t swap/conversion

fzj80-to-1hz-conversion.ai_summary: Early-stage build thread for converting a 1993 FZJ80 from its factory 1FZ gas engine to a 1HZ diesel. Forum members advised that because the 1FZ's H151F gearbox uses coarser splines than the stock 1HZ clutch/flywheel, a 1HDT clutch and flywheel assembly (larger capacity) is needed for the swap. No performance figures or completion updates were present in the thread.

complications.detail: H151F gearbox spline/clutch mismatch with standard 1HZ clutch parts; requires 1HDT clutch and flywheel
Bellhousing compatibility confirmed via HDJ80 sourcing; engine mounts reported as identical between 1FZ and 1HZ

fzj80-to-1hz-conversion.title: Fzj80 to 1hz conversion
fzj80-to-1hz-conversion.transmission: H151F gearbox (carried over from 1FZ) fitted with 1HDT clutch and flywheel for compatibility

midst-of-swap-a442f.ai_summary: New owner acquired an FZJ80 mid-conversion from a previous owner's partially completed 1HZ swap with an Australian-sourced A442F automatic transmission build, and is asking the forum to help finish the job. Outstanding items included wiring for tach/speedo signal sourcing, glow plug relay/timer setup, missing A/C components, and an unclear kickdown cable connection between the injection pump and A442 transmission; the original 1FZ-FE radiator was deemed adequate for cooling.

complications.detail: Tach signal source unclear (injection pump vs fuel pump); speedometer needed conversion using original T-case electronic sensor
Project inherited partially complete from previous owner, with air intake, driveshafts, coolant plumbing, and A/C still needing installation
Kickdown cable from the A442F automatic lacked a clear connection point on the diesel injection pump

midst-of-swap-a442f.title: Bought a FJZ80 in the midst of a 1HZ swap, some questions
midst-of-swap-a442f.transmission: A442F automatic (rebuilt, Australian-sourced Wholesale Automatics valve body and torque converter)

4bt-conversion-duiser.ai_summary: A completed, driven 1993 FZJ80 running a rebuilt Cummins 4BT paired to a rebuilt NV4500 and a rebuilt part-time transfer case, listed for sale with stock electric lockers, a 3-inch lift, and 35s. Listing includes new lift pump, injectors, radiator, alternator, and A/C components; a commenter suggested the engine was still tuned near-stock and could be improved with fuel pin/screw adjustments.
4bt-conversion-duiser.title: FZJ80 Diesel Land Cruiser 4BT Conversion by Duiser
4bt-conversion-duiser.transmission: Rebuilt NV4500 5-speed manual with short-throw shifter kit

93-12v-swap-adapter-kit.ai_summary: Owner of a Japanese-market 1993 FZJ80 is installing a Cummins 5.9L 12-valve pulled from a 1998 Dodge 2500 (190k miles), using a commercial adapter kit from a vendor called Dustin's. As of the thread's last update the build was mid-progress with engine prep underway; no post-swap performance data was reported.

complications.detail: Steering column clearance required fabricating a drop-down brace, with sections cut and re-welded
Fuel pickup tube stability was a concern; forum members recommended hose clamps over the stock pinch clamps, and custom alignment tooling was needed to mate the transmission
Firewall/tunnel clearance was addressed via consideration of a 1-inch body lift

93-12v-swap-adapter-kit.title: 1993 FZJ80 Cummins 5.9 12v Swap
93-12v-swap-adapter-kit.transmission: Stock 80-series gearbox with commercial adapter kit and 1989-05-spec flexplate/adapter plate

96-f4bt80-4l80e.ai_summary: For-sale 1996 FJ80 (owner-labeled 'F4BT80') running a Cummins 3.9L 4BT with P7100 mechanical injection mated to a GM 4L80E automatic with an aftermarket TCI controller. Reported fuel economy of 18-21 mpg highway, 14-16 mpg city, and 13-14 mpg off-road, with extensive overlanding gear and documented maintenance.

complications.detail: 4L80E exhibits fickle lockup/overdrive behavior, requiring a manual torque-converter lockup switch or TCU reprogramming
Factory tachometer is disabled post-swap; a conversion module exists but was not installed
Minor oil leaks noted, addressed via upper/lower gasket replacement

96-f4bt80-4l80e.title: 1996 Cummins Swapped F(Z)J80
96-f4bt80-4l80e.transmission: GM 4L80E automatic with TCI transmission controller

h151-swap-1993.ai_summary: Builder installed a new Cummins R2.8 crate engine into a 1993 FZJ80 mated to the factory H151 5-speed with a custom 3-inch adapter ring, explicitly avoiding any frame cutting/welding. The factory transfer case was retained. R2.8 is rated 161 hp / 310 lb-ft stock.

complications.detail: R2.8 cannot sit as far back as the original 1FZ due to firewall indentation/EGR assembly, requiring a thick custom adapter ring and reworked oil pan sump placement
H151 installation required cutting, fabricating, and welding the transmission tunnel floor
Gasoline fuel lines/tank pickup were incompatible; diesel lines and pickup assembly had to be sourced from a Japan-market 4x4 and the filler pipe required a body lift to remove

h151-swap-1993.title: Cummins R2.8 H151 Swap into 1993 FZJ80

r28-swap-spline-mismatch.ai_summary: Owner of a triple-locked 1995 FZJ80 is planning an R2.8 swap using an Axis/Advanced Adapters bellhousing to an overseas-spec R151F 5-speed, retaining the factory HF2A(V) full-time transfer case. The build stalled on a driveline spline-count mismatch between the transmission output and transfer case input.

complications.detail: Foreign-market R151F output shaft uses 21-23 splines while the HF2A(V) transfer case input requires 19 splines, forcing a choice between modifying the transmission output or the transfer case input, or sourcing an HZJ79/HZJ105 transmission-and-transfer-case combo

r28-swap-spline-mismatch.title: FZJ80 - Cummins r2.8 swap
r28-swap-spline-mismatch.transmission: R151F Toyota 5-speed (foreign-market variant with modified tail housing)

80-series-restoration-ls-swap.ai_summary: 1996 80-series Land Cruiser LS-swapped after a head gasket failure, using a short-crank 2004 LQ4 6.0L machined with a 0.040-inch overbore, paired to a 4WD 4L80E transmission (fitted with a reluctor ring/VSS for Mark's adapter compatibility) and the retained stock transfer case. Engine was completed and installed by September 2025; front and rear driveshafts were being rebuilt for the added torque capacity.

complications.detail: Switching to a Mosely 80-series LS radiator with integrated electric fan for simplified packaging
Front driveshaft needs roughly 3/4-inch shortening and the rear shaft likely needs lengthening; both being rebuilt for higher torque capacity
Original engine wiring harness was unusable; sourced a BP Automotive harness and sent the ECU to LT1Swap for base programming and tach signal modification
Required a GM crank spacer (P/N 12563532) and extended flexplate bolts; engine biased about 1 inch toward the driver side with a 3.5-degree tilt

80-series-restoration-ls-swap.title: My 80 Series Restoration + LS Swap Project

93-lq4-built-4l60e.ai_summary: 1993 FZJ80 swapped with a low-mileage (~40,000 mi) 6.0L LQ4 paired to a built 4L60E Stage 2 transmission, using a Mark's MFK1195AE6 adapter to the retained factory HF2A transfer case. No dyno figures were reported; the build documents mostly exhaust and header fitment troubleshooting.

complications.detail: Old rusted exhaust hangers had to be cut off; Hooker headers (PN 2312HKR) had uneven gasket sealing from a flange design change and were replaced by the manufacturer
Vehicle speed sensor from the original tailshaft required modification to fit the Mark's adapter

93-lq4-built-4l60e.title: 1993 LS Swap (6.0L LQ4 and built 4L60e)
93-lq4-built-4l60e.transmission: Built 4L60E Stage 2 (rated 450hp/500 lb-ft) via Mark's MFK1195AE6 adapter

94-5-3-4l60e-swap.ai_summary: 1994 FZJ80 swap using a low-mileage 2006 Vortec L33 5.3L all-aluminum LS-derived V8 (factory rated 310hp/335 lb-ft) paired to a 2WD 4L60E automatic via a Mark's adapter and spud shaft, retaining the stock full-time transfer case. After PCM tuning the builder estimated output closer to 350hp/350 lb-ft. An F-body oil pan and LS3 exhaust manifolds were fitted along with a custom harness and fuse block.

complications.detail: Aluminum LS block runs hot; required a custom-mounted dual electric fan setup (sourced from a mid-1990s Lincoln Continental) sized to fully cover the stock radiator
Custom wiring harness and fuse block fabricated; MAF sensor intake tube damage discovered during diagnostics
Original Toyota A/C compressor is incompatible with the GM engine mounting; required custom hose fabrication to mate a Denso GM compressor to the existing evaporator/condenser

94-5-3-4l60e-swap.title: 1994 FZJ80 5.3l and 4L60e swap
94-5-3-4l60e-swap.transmission: 2WD 4L60E with Mark's adapter and spud shaft

94-5-3-bumpkinator.ai_summary: 1994 FZJ80 (400k original miles, LHD) swapped with a 2004 Chevy 5.3L Vortec LS (Bryan Tooley Stage 2 cam, deep motor intake) sourced from a 2004 Chevy Avalanche with under 60k miles, paired to a 4L60E with a Stage 2 B&M shift kit. Original engine failed its head gasket. Builder avoided a custom driveshaft by offsetting and raising the engine and using a low-profile Camaro transmission pan plus a flipped front driveline.

complications.detail: Avoided a custom driveshaft by offsetting the engine 3/4in forward and 1/2in toward the driver side, raising it for clearance, using a low-profile transmission pan and Camaro oil pan, and flipping the front driveline

Used an aftermarket wiring harness; modified a Toyota neutral safety switch onto the 4L60E for dash gear-position lights; machined the Toyota coolant temp sensor from 16mm to 12mm threads to fit the LS head port; adapted the Toyota oil pressure sensor with British Standard Pipe threading
Motor mount modifications made using an Advanced Adapters kit

94-5-3-bumpkinator.title: 1994 FZJ80 5.3L swap aka Bumpkinator
94-5-3-bumpkinator.transmission: 4L60E with Stage 2 B&M shift kit and stock converter

94-budget-ls-4l60e.ai_summary: 1994 FZJ80 swap using an LQ4 6.0L pulled from a 2002 GMC Yukon XL Denali (~300k miles, still holding 40psi oil pressure at idle) to replace a 1FZ-FE that blew its head gasket at 300k miles. The donor's AWD 4L60E had the wrong spud shaft, so a separate 2WD 4L60E was sourced and mated to the factory HF2A transfer case via a Mark's 4WD adapter, targeting a sub-$2,000 out-of-pocket budget.

complications.detail: Donor Yukon transmission was an AWD unit with the wrong spud shaft; had to source a separate 2WD 4L60E, and the Mark's 4WD adapter was on a months-long backorder from Advance Adapters
Special oil pan sourced to clear the front driveshaft; universal exhaust manifolds chosen hoping to clear the frame rails
Throttle body converted from drive-by-wire to drive-by-cable; ECU being reprogrammed and harness stripped/simplified

94-budget-ls-4l60e.title: Another One!... 1994 FZJ80 LS/4L60E Swap (Budget, Hopefully)
94-budget-ls-4l60e.transmission: 2WD 4L60E via Mark's 4WD adapter to factory HF2A transfer case

96-ls1-swap-completed-6l90e.ai_summary: Despite the thread title referencing LS1, the builder's own signature clarifies the completed swap in this 1996 FZJ80 (LX450 variant) actually used a 6.2L LS-family engine paired to a 6L90E automatic, with the stock Toyota transfer case and 4WD wiring left functionally unchanged. Dirty Dingo LS street rod motor mounts were used. No dyno numbers were posted, but a test rider described the truck as driving 'smooth as glass' with strong power.

complications.detail: Builder said he'd prefer drive-by-cable over drive-by-wire on a future build to avoid a module failure stranding the truck on trail
Used Dirty Dingo LS street rod motor mounts for engine placement

96-ls1-swap-completed-6l90e.title: 1996 fzj80 LS1 swap completed

fjz80-ls-swap-5-3.ai_summary: 1997 FZJ80 swap using a stock 5.3L Vortec LS pulled from a wrecked 2001 Chevy truck, paired to a 4L60 automatic. Builder wired the whole swap himself and had it professionally tuned for about $500 (upstream O2 sensors only), passing emissions inspection with no check engine light. Reported only a qualitative 'night and day' improvement over the original engine, no dyno numbers.

complications.detail: Builder described doing all the wiring himself as 'the hardest part' of the swap
Stock-appearing shifter retrofitted with custom internal linkage modifications for proper operation

fjz80-ls-swap-5-3.title: FJZ80 LS swap

project-rehab-chopped.ai_summary: Chopped 1994 80-series Land Cruiser (ute conversion) rebuilt around a built LQ4 6.0L Gen III LS V8 (BTR Stage 2 cam, Wiseco pistons, LS7 lifters, head studs, upgraded oiling) paired to a 4L80E automatic and a Mark's 4WD adapter/transfer-case kit. No dyno figures were published in the opening posts, which focus mainly on parts acquisition and build planning.

complications.detail: Fitted an Alloy Works 3-row radiator with electric fans plus separate transmission and power steering coolers
Used a PSI wiring harness with a Cruiser Matt drive-by-wire delete plug
Required Selkirk off-road motor mounts, a custom crossmember, and a Mark's 4WD oil pan/sump pickup kit

project-rehab-chopped.title: Project Rehab (Chopped LS Swapped 80 Series)

96-6bt-conversion.ai_summary: A 1996 HDJ80 owner is swapping in a Cummins 6BT 5.9L sourced from a 1998 Thomas school bus, targeting roughly 300 hp with better reliability than the factory 1HD-T. The bus engine came with an automatic Allison bellhousing/flywheel, so it had to be converted to mate with the Toyota manual gearbox.

complications.detail: Cummins block's factory engine mounts collide with the 80-series firewall, requiring cutting/adapting to a flanged mounting style
Bus-sourced 6BT had an automatic (Allison) flywheel/bellhousing that had to be swapped for manual components
Installed a 450x300x76mm aftermarket intercooler and dual 12-inch electric fans
Integrating factory A/C onto the 6BT was reported as the most difficult retrofit aspect

96-6bt-conversion.title: Toyota '96 HDJ80 - Cummins 6BT conversion
96-6bt-conversion.transmission: H151F manual (retained, converted from donor's automatic Allison flywheel/bellhousing)

prineville-or-listing.ai_summary: Classified listing for a 2021 HZJ79L with its factory 1HZ replaced by a Cummins R2.8, with only about 1,060 km on the vehicle. The listing explicitly states the truck is not licensed/legal for public road use. No transmission, transfer case, or performance figures are given.
prineville-or-listing.title: Prineville, OR: 2021 HZJ79 with Cummins R 2.8

failed-swap-bj74-donor.ai_summary: A 1990 LJ78 owner paid a shop (Land Cruisers Direct) over $17,000 across 16+ months to swap a BJ74's 13B-T and A440F automatic in place of the original 2L-TE. The result was a chronic rough idle (800-1000 rpm), warped harmonic-balancer/drive pulleys, a SPAL cooling fan that kept blowing fuses, and a failing mechanical voltage regulator; after about 4,000 miles the engine lost compression in the forward cylinder. The owner describes the installation quality as poor, with loose/taped-off original wiring bundles and vacuum lines resting on hot surfaces.

complications.detail: SPAL electric fan repeatedly blew fuses/shorted relays; cracked heat-sender housing
Mechanical voltage regulator failed to charge reliably; loose, taped-off original LJ78 harness sections and vacuum lines resting on hot surfaces
Warped harmonic balancer and main drive pulley
Persistent rough idle never resolved; engine lost compression in forward cylinder after ~4,000 miles despite claimed compression testing by the shop

failed-swap-bj74-donor.title: lj78 13bt Failed swap, need advice

1990-prado-70-series-build.ai_summary: This 1990 LJ78 build thread documents a 1KZ-TE swap replacing the original 2L-T, while keeping the stock LJ78 manual gearbox, ECU, and wiring harness (which the builder himself calls 'a bit of an abomination'). Differentials were upgraded to KZJ78-spec units for a slightly higher ratio and to gain rear diff-lock capability, and the truck runs 31-inch Yokohama A/T tires. The vehicle remained a functioning daily driver used for river crossings and rock crawling, though the builder reported ongoing fuel-delivery underperformance affecting acceleration.

complications.detail: Original LJ78 ECU and wiring retained despite the 1KZ-TE swap, creating a mismatched setup; also recurring seal-beam headlight fuse blowing
Fuel delivery system underperformance reducing acceleration versus expectations; rear axle seal failure addressed during the build

1990-prado-70-series-build.title: 1990 Landcruiser Prado 70 series Build

ash-awbery-surf-a343f.ai_summary: Owner (Ash Awbery) swapped a Hilux Surf-sourced 1KZ-TE into an LJ78, keeping the A343F automatic via the Surf's bellhousing/torque converter and running 4.88 diffs with 35-inch tires. Running the 1KZ-TE's electronic injection pump off the original 2L-TE ECU caused white smoke, unburnt fuel, and high idle; the fix was fitting a 4M40 manual injection pump. He planned to eventually 'manualise' the drivetrain and add a Spitronics ECU for transmission control.

complications.detail: 2L-TE ECU incompatible with 1KZ-TE electronic injection pump (10mm vs 12mm pump fueling mismatch), causing white smoke and high idle despite potentiometer tuning attempts
2L-TE engine mounts required modification, but Surf bellhousing/torque converter bolted to the A343F with no major issues

ash-awbery-surf-a343f.title: LJ78 to 1kzte

engine-conversion-mechanical-pump.ai_summary: After the original 2L-TE failed in this automatic LJ78, the owner proceeded with a 1KZ-TE swap using a mechanically-converted injector pump rather than the stock electronic pump. Forum members recommended a good exhaust and intercooler to control EGTs, with some debate over 1KZ head-gasket reliability (one vendor reported past head issues, others defended the engine as reliable with proper maintenance). The thread ends with the owner asking about control units for running the automatic transmission with the swapped engine, indicating the install proceeded but with less documented outcome detail than other threads.

complications.detail: Multiple posters recommended intercooler and improved exhaust to manage EGTs on the 1KZ conversion
Owner still seeking a control-unit solution for the automatic transmission after the mechanical-pump 1KZ-TE swap
Disputed reliability track record cited: one vendor reported head-gasket issues on prior 1KZ conversions

engine-conversion-mechanical-pump.intercooler: recommended for EGT management alongside a mechanical injection pump conversion (no specific product confirmed)
engine-conversion-mechanical-pump.title: LJ78 engine conversion

rusi-rusev-530d-donor.ai_summary: Forum user Rusi Rusev swapped a BMW M57 turbodiesel inline-6 (pulled complete with wiring/ECU/pedal/keys from a 2003 BMW 530D) into his Toyota LJ78 Prado, replacing the original 2L-TE. The stock Toyota gearbox was retained using a custom bellhousing built from the BMW bell, with axle ratios changed to 41/10 rear (from a 4Runner 1KZ) and 14/10 front (from an 80-series) to suit the new powerband. Owner reported 0-100km/h in about 11 seconds, 160km/h top speed, and fuel consumption of 9-11 L/100km.

complications.detail: Custom bellhousing fabricated from a BMW bell housing to mate the M57 to the stock LJ78 Toyota gearbox; radiator repositioned about 20mm forward to clear the engine
Turbo diesel charge-air cooling handled with an intercooler sourced from a Range Rover P38
Rear axle ratio changed to 41/10 (from a 4Runner 1KZ) and front to 14/10 (from an 80-series Land Cruiser) to match the M57's power delivery
Wiring kept as an intact BMW harness/ECU package - owner advised pulling the engine complete with all cables, computer, gas pedal, and keys from the donor to simplify integration
